title: AlphaProteo: High-Affinity De Novo Protein Binder Design
whyItMatters: Designs custom disease-targeting protein binders in silico with up to 10× tighter wet-lab affinity and 88% hit rates—eliminating rounds of experimental evolution.
summary: Google DeepMind unveiled AlphaProteo, an AI system capable of generating novel high-affinity protein binders for challenging biomedical targets including VEGF-A (cancer and diabetic retinopathy), SARS-CoV-2 spike, IL-7Rα, and TrkA. Wet-lab experiments demonstrated 3× to 300× stronger binding affinities than prior computational design methods and up to 88% experimental success on target BHRF1—without post-design lab optimization.
technicalHighlights: First AI system to design a successful de novo binder for VEGF-A, a clinically vital angiogenesis target.
Achieved ~10× stronger average binding affinity than state-of-the-art computational protein design pipelines.
Validated directly in wet-lab biophysical assays across seven diverse disease-linked proteins.
caveats: Did not succeed on all tested targets (e.g., TNFα proved refractory), and clinical translation still requires immunogenicity, stability, and delivery optimization.
contributors: Google DeepMind Protein Design & Wet Lab Teams

scoreRationale.foundational: Demonstrates reliable zero-shot functional molecular design directly from target structure.
scoreRationale.ripple: Accelerates biologics, diagnostic biosensors, oncology therapeutics, and antiviral countermeasure development.
scoreRationale.verification: Backed by direct experimental wet-lab validation across multiple independent protein targets.
scoreRationale.velocity: Replaces months of iterative phage-display and affinity-maturation cycles with single-shot AI generation.
